mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 1.5% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the horizon are not statistically lower than during a similar period of stable or declining rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns within 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by > 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite the labor indicators meeting the specified trigger (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (not available in provided proxies; fallback to HOUST as proxy for demand) and industrial production (INDPRO) above trend for three months indicates expanding economic activity, which elevates equity risk appetite and produces positive 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and INDPRO both exceed their 6-month moving averages for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when demand proxies meet the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound above the prior contraction level within one month suggests resolving supply bottlenecks, which reduces uncertainty and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO shows two consecutive months of contraction followed by a rebound month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the supply signal meeting the trigger (t-test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the annual inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates aggressive rate hikes, causing a sharp decline in equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the inflation trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining consumer payrolls (PAYEMS) for four consecutive months indicates weakening labor demand, which can lead to reduced consumer spending and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases month-over-month for four consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a comparable four-month payrolls expansion (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining Treasury yields (inferred from FEDFUNDS < 2%) suggest central bank accommodation, which typically precedes equity market rallies and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the low-yield period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rapid decline below the spike level within one trading day suggests temporary supply disruptions, creating uncertainty that drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO spikes above 100 (example threshold) and falls below within the same trading day
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when the supply shock trigger is detected.
